plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This holds because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $28, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding higher than my value risks winning and overpaying above what the item is worth to me. Bidding lower risks losing auctions I should win at a profitable price. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $23.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values uniformly distributed on [0,49]. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy: since the price paid depends only on the second-highest bid (not my own bid, given I win), overbidding risks paying more than my value, and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, regardless of the other bidders' strategies, I should bid exactly my value of $36 to maximize expected profit.
